'''Middlesbrough Football Club''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=en-uk-Middlesbrough.ogg|ˈ|m|ɪ|d|əl|z|b|r|ə}} {{respell|MID|əlz|brə}}) is a professional [[association football]] club based in [[Middlesbrough]], [[North Yorkshire]]. They compete in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]], the second tier of [[English football league system|English football]]. Nicknamed "'''the Boro'''", they were formed in 1876 and are the 12th [[List of football clubs in England and Wales by year formed|oldest football league club]] in England and Wales. The club have played at the [[Riverside Stadium]] since 1995,<ref name="RSStadium">{{cite web |url=http://www.gazettelive.co.uk/boro-fc/boro-club-info/ |title=Boro FC club info |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070904115147/http://www.gazettelive.co.uk/boro-fc/boro-club-info/ |archive-date=4 September 2007 |publisher=gazettelive.co.uk |access-date=27 May 2008}}</ref> having previously played at [[Ayresome Park]] for 92 years, from 1903 to 1995.

Middlesbrough were one of the founding members of the [[Premier League]] in 1992, and have spent all but two seasons of their entire history as a professional club competing within the top two tiers of English football.<ref name="MFCHistBk1"/> Their highest league finish to date was third place in the top flight in the [[1913–14 in English football|1913–14 season]]. The outbreak of the [[World War I|First World War]] stunted their push for a first top division title, though the club pushed again during the inter-war years, finishing fourth in the [[1938–39 Football League|1938–39 season]] before the [[World War II|Second World War]] halted the English leagues and again prevented a push for a first title. The club came within minutes of folding in 1986 before they were saved by a [[consortium]] led by board member and later chairman [[Steve Gibson (businessman)|Steve Gibson]].<ref name="PremierLeagueSite"/> A remarkable [[Middlesbrough F.C. survival from liquidation|recovery]] saw the club immediately earn back-to-back promotions to the top division in the [[1986–87 Middlesbrough F.C. season|1986–87]] and [[1987–88 Middlesbrough F.C. season|1987–88]] seasons. The club were runners-up in the [[FA Cup]] and [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] in 1997<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/middlesbrough-199697-rucks-relegation-cup-finals-and-training-a-prison|title=Middlesbrough 1996/97: rucks, relegation, cup finals... and training at a prison|last=Stewart|first=Rob|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=30 January 2017|access-date=5 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/middlesbroughs-surreal--draining-dream-18048235|title=Middlesbrough's surreal draining 'Dream Time' 96/97 season still shapes fans' emotions|last=Vickers|first=Anthony|publisher=[[TeessideLive]]|date=6 April 2020|access-date=5 September 2022}}</ref> while also being relegated following a controversial 3-point deduction,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/middlesbrough-rocked-by-threepoint-penalty-1283330.html|title=Middlesbrough rocked by three-point penalty|last=Duxbury|first=Nick|publisher=[[The Independent|Independent]]|date=15 January 1997|access-date=23 February 2024}}</ref> and losing another League Cup [[1998 Football League Cup final|final]] the following season. Under [[Steve McClaren]], the club won the League Cup in [[2004 Football League Cup final|2004]], its first major silverware, and reached the [[2006 UEFA Cup final]]. The club has played one Premier League season since relegation in 2009.

Middlesbrough is the only major professional football club in the greater [[Teesside]] area (the 14th biggest [[List of urban areas in the United Kingdom|urban area]] in England), the [[Tees Valley]], and the county of [[North Yorkshire]] (the largest county in England by area<ref name="English Counties By Population And Area 2024">{{cite web |url=http://populationdata.org.uk/english-counties-by-population-and-area/ |title= English Counties By Population And Area 2024 |date= 27 August 2021 |publisher=populationdata.org |access-date=22 March 2024}}</ref>). The club has regional rivalries with [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United F.C]] (the [[Tyne–Tees derby]]) and [[Sunderland A.F.C.]] (the [[Tees–Wear derby]]).<ref name="fan survey">{{cite web |url=http://www.footballfanscensus.com/issueresults/Club_Rivalries_Uncovered_Results.pdf |title=Club rivalries uncovered |publisher=footballfancensus |access-date=13 October 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020074918/http://www.footballfanscensus.com/issueresults/Club_Rivalries_Uncovered_Results.pdf |archive-date=20 October 2013 }}</ref>

The club's traditional kit is red with white detailing, often in the form of a white chest band. The home shorts and sock colours have interchangeably been shifted between red and white, complementing the red shirt that was adopted in 1899.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://historicalkits.co.uk/Middlesbrough/Middlesbrough.htm|title=Middlesbrough historical kits|publisher=Historicalkits.co.uk|access-date=12 June 2019}}</ref> The various crests throughout the club's history, the most recent of which was adopted in 2026,<ref name="newcrest">{{cite news |date=12 May 2007 |url=http://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/1392479.boro_change_badge_to_reflect_history/ |title=Boro change badge to reflect history |work=The Northern Echo |access-date=10 October 2008 |first=Matt |last=Westcott | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081207104857/http://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/1392479.boro_change_badge_to_reflect_history/ | archive-date=7 December 2008 | url-status=live }}</ref> incorporates a lion within a roundel crest linking to Teesside landmarks. For the 2026–27 season this has been made golden with 150 years printed below it."}}
